results.title: AdAnt AI: Muse for Social Media Marketing | Product Hunt
results.content:
#### What needs improvement

The feedback loop is the obvious gap. Right now once you push a creative live, you're manually tracking what performs and bringing that insight back in yourself. A closed loop where ad performance data feeds directly into the next round of strategy would make this genuinely hard to compete with. Also a pay-as-you-go credit option for lighter users would remove a lot of friction at the top of funnel.

#### vs Alternatives

Tried AdCreative.ai before this and found it leaned too generic. The outputs looked fine but didn't really map to what was working in our specific category. AdAnt felt different because it actually grounds the strategy in niche-level data, not platform-wide trends that could be saturated by the time you publish.

#### What's great

What stands out about AdAnt is that it goes beyond simply generating an AI video. It helps bridge the gap between creative strategy and production by breaking down references, suggesting hooks and angles, and turning them into multiple ad variations for testing. For our team at Acti, this makes it much easier to move from an initial idea to testable short-form creatives without coordinating several different tools.

#### What needs improvement [...] #### What needs improvement

I’d love to see more precise control over individual scenes, captions, pacing, and brand elements after the first draft is generated. A clearer comparison view for different hooks and creative variants would also make it easier for teams to review, select, and organize experiments before launching them.

#### vs Alternatives

We also considered Creatify and other AI video generators. We chose AdAnt because its conversational, strategy-first workflow felt better suited to creative iteration. Instead of starting from a blank prompt every time, we could work from a product URL or reference ad, explore different hooks and angles, and generate variations within the same workflow.

results.title: The Real Struggle with AI Coding Agents — And How to Overcome It
results.content:
Yes, I could scroll back through the chat history, find the fix, and apply it manually. But by that point, I was usually too frustrated (or too lazy) to do it myself. It was easier to just tell the AI, “Hey, that bug is back,” and let it fix it again — which, of course, meant spending more credits on something I’d technically already paid for once.

## Why These Problems Happen

When you first hit these roadblocks with an AI coding agent, it’s easy to blame the tool. “This AI is broken.” “It doesn’t understand my project.” “It’s making stupid mistakes.”

But after working with multiple agents over time, I realized these issues weren’t random. They follow patterns — and once you understand the root causes, you can predict them and even prevent a lot of them before they happen. [...] It’s like walking into a house that someone built for you overnight. You didn’t choose where the light switches go, why the bathroom is on the other side of the kitchen, or why there’s a door that doesn’t seem to lead anywhere. And now you have to live in it.

### Small Changes Breaking Everything

One of the most frustrating patterns I noticed was the “butterfly effect” of changes. I’d ask the AI to tweak something tiny — say, adjust a form layout or update a validation rule — and suddenly, unrelated features would break.

results.title: AdAnt AI Review & Alternative (2026) — ViralMojo
results.content:
AdAnt AI (adant.ai, by AnyLoop Inc, San Jose) is an agentic social video tool that launched on Product Hunt in August 2026 as the #1 product of its day. It runs three agents: a Content Strategy agent that researches what's winning in your niche across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and competitors' Meta ads and turns it into a strategy report; a Social Video agent that recreates any short you paste in — or one of its shot-by-shot analyzed templates — with your product and AI avatars; and a Social Manager agent that schedules, posts and reports back (posting is in beta). It's aimed at B2C and DTC brands, apps and creators, and its headline claims are 50M+ organic views, 10K+ winning ads created and a 60% CAC reduction on ads. Pricing is credit-based — Standard $15, Pro $39, Max $99 to $999 a [...] Comparison pages have a trust problem — most shade the truth. Every competitor fact on this page is checked against public sources on the date shown, the ✕ marks on our own side are real, and the ads in the receipts table are public links you can verify. If anything here is out of date or unfair to the competitor, tell me and I'll fix it.
